name: Jōmon pottery
summary: The oldest pottery of Japan. Hunter-gatherers coiled a coarse clay into deep pots, pressed twisted cord into the wet wall, and fired the pots in an open bonfire.

philosophy.core_thesis: A pot is a coiled and fired form that carries the marks of its making: the cord, the cut and the clay itself are the ornament.
design_principles: Build the pot from clay coils 15 to 25 mm thick and smooth only the inside.
Roll twisted cord across the wet outer wall to leave a dense, even texture.
Keep the pot deep: the height is one to two times the mouth width.
Fire the pot in an open bonfire at 600 to 900 °C, with no kiln and no glaze.
Raise the rim of a ceremonial pot into a crown of clay loops, handles and spikes.
Divide the surface into bands: cord-marked, incised, and plain zones that alternate.
Leave the clay body in its fired colour, from buff to dark brown, with black fire clouds.
anti_patterns: A glossy glaze or any liquid surface on the wall
A smooth thrown wall with the rings of the wheel
A flat base with a turned foot ring
Thin even walls less than 5 mm thick
Painted pictures of people or animals in colour

form.shape: A deep cooking and storage pot with a round or pointed base and a mouth that is as wide as the belly or wider.
form.profile: An S-curve or a straight cylinder; flame-style pots narrow at the waist and open into a tall crown at the rim.
form.foot_and_rim: A rounded or small flat base; the rim carries applied loops, curls and four large handles on the ceremonial pots.
form.proportion: Height 30 to 60 cm, mouth 25 to 45 cm, and a wall 8 to 20 mm thick.
rules: Make the base pointed or round for a pot that stands in ash or sand.
Build the crown on the rim in four symmetrical groups of loops.
Keep the wall thick and uneven; the coil joins stay visible inside.
Place the densest ornament at the rim and the shoulder.

bodies.rule: Use a coarse local clay with sand, mica or plant fibre. The body is porous and soft, and it stays dark and uneven after the fire.

forming.joins: Coils are pressed together and blended with wet fingers; handles and rim loops are rolled and pressed on with slip.
forming.details: Cord, rope and shell impressions on the wall, finger-tip marks along the rim, and a dark patch where the fire touched the surface.

glaze.pattern: Twisted cord rolled in bands, then incised curves, spirals and bold ridges; the flame-style rim is a crown of applied clay.
glaze.gloss: Dry matt, below 5 GU; no glaze covers the body.
glaze.wear: The surface is chalky and soft; the cord texture and the fire clouds stay clear after thousands of years.

palette.strategy: Earth tones from the clay and the fire only: buff, brown and black, with no added colour.

firing.kiln: An open bonfire or a shallow pit with wood, grass and dry bark as fuel; there is no kiln.
processes: dry the pot for several days
stack the pots in a pit
fire in the open for a few hours
firing.scale: A household or a village made the pots by hand, one at a time, in a few dozen pieces for each season.
firing.signs: Uneven colour, black fire clouds, a soft chalky wall and visible coil joins.

pieces.form: Cylindrical deep pot with a pointed base and cord marks over the whole wall
Flame-style vessel with four rim crowns of clay loops and incised spirals
Large burial jar with a plain neck and cord-marked belly
Plain small pot with a smooth wall and one handle, for daily use

lineage.root: It is among the earliest fired clay in the world, and no earlier style in this data leads to it.

emotion.target_response: A deep, ancient energy: the viewer sees clay that people shaped by hand long before writing and feels its weight and force.

use_cases: a museum label for prehistoric Japanese ware

a prompt for an archaeology scene with fired clay

the brief wants a thin, refined or white body

modifiers.how: Change to a fine stoneware body, add a thin green glaze and a neat foot, and fire in a kiln at 1200 °C.
Keep the coiled form and the rough clay, add a plain glaze and a functional shape.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Jōmon culture

wall_thickness.note: Jōmon walls are thick and uneven; they are never thin.
